title: damages_range_v1
description: What a claim of this shape against a production actually resolves for, researched rather than assumed. The severity table in policy/exposure.yaml was written from general knowledge; this asks the record instead. Court dockets carry judgments but almost never settlements, so the answer here comes from legal commentary, media law reporting, insurance and E&O industry writing, and reported matters -- secondary sources, which is how a practitioner answers this question too. The schema makes the researcher say which kind of source it found, so a figure from an insurance loss study and a figure from one famous verdict never render as the same thing.

range_found.description: Whether the record supports a range at all. False is a real answer and must not be rendered as zero.

outcome.description: Which resolution this range describes. A settlement range and a tried-to-verdict range are different numbers about different events and must not be averaged together.

typical_usd.description: The figure the record treats as ordinary, where it says so. Usually far below the reported headline cases.

defence_cost_usd.description: What defending costs regardless of outcome. The most knowable number here: it is billed hourly against published rates and does not depend on anyone's confidential settlement.

source_kind.description: What the range rests on. `single_notable_case` is the weakest and the most likely to be found, because the outlier matters are the ones that get written about; a figure from one famous verdict must never be presented as typical.

outlier_warning.description: Set when the figures found are dominated by a handful of famous matters rather than a body of ordinary ones. This is the expected condition in this field, and saying so is the difference between research and an anecdote.

basis.description: What the range actually rests on, in a sentence. The field that decides whether a producer may be shown the number.

confidence_note.description: Why the range is wide or narrow. Most of these matters resolve confidentially, so a wide range is frequently the honest answer and a narrow one usually means the record is thin rather than the amount certain.
